About

Andy Rochmol is an 11-year-old pianist and composer whose artistic voice moves fluently between classical repertoire, original composition, and crossover performance. Fluent in English and Spanish, with early studies in German, he connects with audiences across the United States, Latin America, and beyond.

Andy began exploring music at two and made his stage debut as a drummer at three. At five, he composed his first original piece — "Papá Cielo" — written to comfort his father. His teachers have consistently remarked on his ability to absorb and implement corrections at the piano with unusual depth, often reshaping a passage after a single note. That same drive to create has led him to teach himself to read and write in alto clef and to transpose for instruments such as the French horn and clarinet — skills most young musicians encounter much later, if at all. In 2024, that curiosity took shape in his first string quartet, recorded by professional musicians from Bellas Artes in Mexico City.

In December 2025, Andy premiered the first movement of his original symphony in New York City. The full recording was completed in April 2026 and is currently being mixed in Spain — his most ambitious work to date. New York also gave him something he didn't expect: he walked into Carnegie Hall for the first time, and it became the stage he dreams of. His growing presence in the professional world has drawn support from names like Fazioli, who backed his attendance at NAMM 2026, and Studiologic, who recognized his artistry by providing him with one of their flagship instruments — a keyboard that bridges the feel of a concert piano with the expressive range a jazz and contemporary performer needs.

Andy currently studies with Mauricio Náder, concert pianist at Bellas Artes in Mexico. During the summer of 2025, he attended the Musicians Institute Summer Shot in Los Angeles on a full scholarship, the Kutztown Summer Music Festival in Pennsylvania, and the Piano Seminar at the Music Society of San Miguel de Allende — working closely with world-class faculty including Sean Kennard (Steinway Artist), Gile Bae (Steinway Artist), Maria Asteriadou (Manhattan School of Music), and Dr. Daniel Immel.

"Andy is an exceptional case. His musicality, interpretive maturity, and creative capacity at such a young age are simply admirable."

— Mauricio Náder, Concert Pianist, Bellas Artes México
